Senses.PreferredTarget: give the cue to suit the occasion
AlternateTargets: call the tune according to the company
adapt the performance to the seat
Senses.Note: Four differently evaluated performances establish “give the cue to suit the occasion” across four independent works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不若相席打令，曲順時宜，道箇沃雪庵前新水滿，趙家橋畔綠陰多
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB202.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄). English Label: Baichi Yuanshuo prefers fitting the cue to the occasion and then voices a locally apt scene. Canonical roster link: Baichi Xingyuan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 然則相席打令，似有知音。鏤骨銘心，罕逢明鑑。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1307.xml). Wansong's Comments on Tiantong's Further Inquiries (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚拈古請益錄). English Label: Wansong Xingxiu comments that adapting the cue to the company seems to find a listener who knows the tune.

Occurrences.Kwic: 天童恁麼判斷，雖則相席打令，猶是大嚼對屠門。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X64/X64n1260.xml). Outline Record of the Successive Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄). English Label: Muchen Daomin judges Tiantong's situationally fitted cue still to be like chewing grandly before a butcher's gate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 適逢諸開士相席打令，欲老僧鼓兩片皮、弄三寸舌，說禪說道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄). English Label: Poshan Haiming describes the practitioners as adjusting cues to one another and wanting him to exercise his lips and tongue.

Senses.Explanation: Give the cue to suit the occasion describes words adjusted to the present company or seat. Baichi uses it before speaking of local water and shade; Wansong pairs it with seeming to have a listener who knows the tune; Muchen concedes it to Tiantong's judgment but compares that judgment to chewing before a butcher's gate; and Poshan applies it to practitioners prompting one another to speak.
